chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far al-Kumaydani narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said:

Among the signs of the jurisprudent are patience (forbearance), knowledge, and silence. Indeed, silence is one of the gates of wisdom, and indeed, silence acquires affection, and indeed, it is a guide for every good.

key_terms.فقه: Jurisprudence / deep understanding of religious law

ai.seo_question: What are the three signs of a true jurisprudent according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) defines the essence of *Fiqh* not merely as legal technicality but as a spiritual state characterized by *Hilm* (forbearance), *Ilm* (knowledge), and *Samt* (silence). This aligns with the Shia scholarly tradition where silence is viewed as an active discipline that preserves wisdom and fosters social harmony, serving as a practical indicator of inner piety. The emphasis on silence reflects the Prophetic tradition that 'silence is the key to wisdom,' distinguishing the true jurisprudent from the verbose.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-202 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Musa ibn Abi Ja’far al-Kumaydany quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty that Abul Hassan Al-Ridha (MGB) said, “
Patience, knowledge and silence are among the signs of the jurisprudent. Silence is one of the gates of wisdom. Silence attracts affection and is a guide for any good affair.”
